messages:
marie: Heads-up — after turning on FlashAttention kernel selection by default for the Llama-3 family, we saw a drop in aggregate throughput for short-chat workloads. Suspect interaction with paged KV and our continuous batching heuristics. Any quick thoughts?

raj: Saw the same. Profiling shows fewer tokens/batch and higher dispatch overhead. Tail latency up ~35ms for 0-64 token requests.

jen: Do we have profiles that break down time spent in attention kernel vs KV page fetch? Could be kernel faster per-token but forces smaller batches due to seq_len handling.

raj: Yes — quick snippet from the perf trace:
```
model: llama-3-8b-v1
avg_seq: 24
avg_tokens_per_req: 18
flash_attn_time: 6.2ms (per-token normalized)
paged_kv_fetch: 9.8ms (per-request)
batch_formation_time: 4.1ms
queue_wait: 12.6ms
```
Notice paged_kv_fetch is almost constant per request and dominates when batches are small.

sam: Sounds like token budget per batch is too aggressive for short requests. If paged KV has a fixed cost, we need to bias batch formation toward request count over token-sum for low-seq workloads.

marie: Agreed. Current continuous batching config: max_batch_size=64, token_budget=1024, hold_time_ms=8, queue_policy=TOKEN_PRIORITY. That policy prioritizes grouping by token budget which may fragment short requests.

lucas: Suggest experiment: set queue_policy=COUNT_PRIORITY for seq_len < 128, and add an adaptive hold_time that increases for tiny requests (hold_time_ms -> 12). Also try token_budget=2048 to encourage larger batches.

toni: Also we can add a flash fallback: prefer FlashAttention for seq_len >= 128, otherwise use cached standard kernel that cooperates better with batching and paged KV. That avoids micro-batch churn for small seqs.

jen: +1 on adaptive kernel selection. Implementation idea: routing layer estimates seq_len at enqueue, attaches preferred_kernel tag. Batcher respects tag when assembling batch; if mixed, fall back to generic kernel.

ops-bot: Experiment started: AB test A=default, B=COUNT_PRIORITY + hold_time 12ms + kernel-fallback rule. Patch: deploy/2026-03-17/batch-tuning-BETA.

raj: I ran a quick sim with synthetic 1-64 token traffic. Results: throughput +8%, p95 latency -20ms, but p50 unchanged. Memory usage slightly up due to larger batches (kv page reuse improved).

marie: Great. Can we also add a metric for "kv_page_per_request" so we can detect when paged-KV fixed cost is the bottleneck? If that rises, autoswitch policies.

sam: I'll instrument that and add a dashboard tile. For rollout, recommend canary to 5% of production short-req traffic for 3 hours, collect: tokens_per_batch, batch_size_count, kv_page_per_req, p95_tail.

lucas: One more gotcha — FlashAttention's fused kernels can increase memory pressure when combined with larger batches, causing occasional OOMs on 24GB GPUs. We'll set an OOM guard: if free_mem < 2GB then force standard kernel.

marie: Plan: 1) Canary B (ops-bot), 2) collect new metrics, 3) add kernel fallback threshold rules + OOM guard, 4) iterate. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

jen: Also log an issue with model onboarding notes so future model teams know to flag paged-KV heavy patterns.

raj: I'll follow up with a short perf write-up and attach the flamegraphs.

marie: Perfect. Closing loop once canary finishes.
